email_enabled.description:
Whether outgoing email is configured; gates password reset and
email settings in the interface.

AuthorizationResponse.description: An application the user has live access tokens for.

created_at.description: When the oldest live token was issued.

expires_at.description: When the newest live token expires; the client must re-authorise then.

scopes.description: Every scope any of the live tokens carries.

build_path.description: Directory Dokploy builds from, such as `/` or `/web`.

compose_path.description: Compose file relative to the repository root, such as `./compose.yml`.

kind.description: `application` for a Dockerfile, `compose` for a Compose file.

port.description: The port the Dockerfile exposes, or the chosen Compose service's port.

service.description: The Compose service a domain should route to.

services.description: Every service in a Compose file, with the port it listens on if known.

warnings.description: Things in the file that commonly break a Dokploy deployment.

volume_id.description:
`None` for object storage and external databases, which sit on no
volume this host can see.

CommitEmailVerification.description: How an address came to count, or why it does not yet.

account_email.description: The account address, which counts without being listed.

author_name.description: The name and address browser commits actually use.

primary_email.description: The chosen address for browser commits, if any.

verification_required.description:
Whether new addresses must be confirmed by email before they count.
False when the instance cannot send mail.

CommitRefResponse.description: A tag or release pointing at a commit, for decorating history rows.

commits_since_previous.description:
Commits between the previous release and this one, for releases whose
predecessor is known.

contexts.description: Statuses reported by external CI through the commit status API.

state.description: GitHub names the field `state`; Gitea also accepts it.

DayCommitResponse.description: A commit listed under one day of a namespace's activity graph.

summary.description: The provider's description of what it started.

DeploymentSuggestionsResponse.description: What a repository can deploy, read from its default branch.

project_name.description: Default name for a new remote project.

workflow.description: Workflow path, such as `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml`, or its file name.

active_target_id.description: `None` while the domain uses its local root.

email_enabled.description: Whether the instance can send mail at all.

credential.description: WebAuthn credential from the browser; external browser protocol.

MigrationRequest.description:
Selects the destination of a migration. `local` selects the domain's
local root; so does the nil `target_id`, which older clients send.

target_id.description: Nil when the destination is the local root.

MigrationView.description:
One migration's progress, as returned by the progress endpoint and sent by
its event stream.

repository_count.description: Repositories the viewer may read that contributed to the graph.

scope.description:
`person` counts the commits the user wrote anywhere; `organization`
counts every commit in its repositories.

repositories.description: Repositories with commits that day, busiest first.

options.description: WebAuthn request options from webauthn-rs; external browser protocol.

id.description:
The stored token hash. It identifies the invitation without revealing
the token that redeems it.

ReauthenticationRequest.description:
Either proof is enough to change an enabled second factor: the password
covers a lost authenticator and the code covers a forgotten password.

commit_oid.description:
The commit the ref resolves to. For an annotated tag this differs from
`oid`, which is the tag object, so decorating commits needs this one.

problem.description: Why this provider cannot be used by this Gitadel, if it cannot.

targets_instance.description: False when the provider was configured for another forge.

RepositoryUsage.description:
Stored data one repository owns in one domain. `total_bytes` counts
persisted objects; temporary data belongs in `details`.

current_password.description:
Required when the request uses an API token, because a verified
address can reset the password.

SetupDeploymentResponse.description: The outcome of a one-step deployment setup.

warning.description: A later step that failed after the resource was linked.

project_id.description: An existing remote project; otherwise `project_name` is created.
An existing remote project; otherwise `project_name` is created.

SourceCheckResponse.description: Whether Dokploy can list repositories through the bound provider.

attempts.description: Addresses that failed, in the order they were tried.

internal_url.description: The Gitadel address Dokploy uses after the check.

check.description: Set when this response follows a reachability check.

status.description: Gitea's field name for the same value.

StorageTargetCapacity.description:
What the underlying volume holds, for targets that sit on one. Object stores
publish no capacity, so S3 targets leave this empty rather than inventing a
ceiling.

resource.description: Provider-owned resource link; `null` unlinks, absent leaves it.

UsageDetail.description:
A domain-specific counter reported beside object count and bytes, such as
the registry's tag count.

per_repository.description: Whether the counter is meaningful per repository, or only as a total.

UsageUnit.description: How a usage detail is measured, so clients can format it.

Volume.description:
A mounted filesystem holding at least one category. `used_bytes` counts
everything on it, Gitadel included; space the filesystem keeps back for
root is neither used nor available, so it is reported on its own instead
of making the other figures fail to add up.

attempts.description: Attempts made so far, including the one in flight.

next_attempt_at.description: When a delivery that is waiting to be retried is next attempted.

info.description: REST API. Paths are relative to /api/v1. Errors use {error: {code, message}}. Git, registry, OAuth token and runner protocols are separate.
